name: ffpng
baseline: image-rs/image-png v0.18.1 (Rust PNG decoder with fdeflate, built with --features=unstable); the same harness also times libpng + zlib, libspng, stb_image and libdeflate-backed inflate, but the README publishes no libpng or libspng numbers
workload: PNG decode of the whole QOI benchmark suite (2848 images in 13 categories), single core pinned at real-time priority with boost off, geometric mean MP/s and per-image ratio against image-png, output checked byte for byte.
claimed_speedup: Overall 1.115x faster than image-png on a Ryzen 7950X (356.3 vs 319.5 MP/s geomean) and 1.204x faster on a Ryzen 9950X3D (352.6 vs 292.8 MP/s); faster in all 13 categories, from 1.024x (photo_wikipedia, 9950X3D) to 1.827x (screenshot_web, 9950X3D). README says decode speed is about 3% ahead on dense photographs.
compiler_and_flags: gcc 16.1 (7950X run) and gcc 16.2.1 (9950X3D run) targeting x86-64-v3 (AVX2, BMI2, PCLMUL); image-png at target-cpu=x86-64-v3 on Rust nightly (1.98.0-nightly c1b22f44c for the follow-up); clang builds run about 10% slower per README
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X and Ryzen 9 9950X3D, one isolated core (isolcpus, nohz_full), taskset plus chrt -f 99, CPU boost off
tradeoffs: Single header ffpng.h, C99, libc plus immintrin.h only. Decode only (no encoder). Requires x86-64-v3 (AVX2, BMI2, PCLMUL; Intel since 2013, AMD since 2017); not portable to ARM. Output is fixed to 8-bit samples (EXPAND and STRIP_16: 16-bit truncated to the high byte). Handles all PNG color types, depths and interlacing.
caveats: The win is over the previous state of the art (image-png), not over libpng; the README says the harness times libpng, libspng and stb_image but does not print their numbers, so the libpng speedup is not stated on the page. 16-bit PNGs are truncated to 8 bits, the same semantics as image-png (EXPAND and STRIP_16) but not libpng default output. Corpus (QOI benchmark suite) is not vendored. Absolute throughput requires core isolation and boost off. Very new repository (first commit 2026-06-23). Source header carries an SPDX MIT tag and a copyright line but the repository has no LICENSE file.
found_via: GitHub topic page github.com/topics/image-decoder sorted by recently updated (description 'faster than image-png on the QOI corpus'); README cites the image-rs blog post 'fastest PNG decoder in the world' (post itself not opened)

name: QLIC (Quick Lossless Image Codec)
baseline: libjxl lossless (JPEG XL effort 9) and libwebp lossless (preset 6); also OxiPNG level 6
workload: Lossless encode and decode of a 3,167-image corpus (1,964,362,720 pixels: DIV2K and CLIC 2022 validation, QOI benchmark categories, Enrico UI screenshots), one pinned logical processor, byte-exact roundtrip check on every file.
claimed_speedup: Encode: QLIC automatic policy 618.673 s vs JPEG XL lossless effort 9 5,674.173 s (about 9.2x faster, derived from page data) and vs OxiPNG level 6 9,105.634 s (about 14.7x, derived), with 1,160,913,984 bytes total vs 1,164,424,898 (JPEG XL e9) and 1,289,518,274 (WebP preset 6). Decode: QLIC 236.927 s (8.291 MP/s) vs JPEG XL effort 9 files 307.602 s (29.83% slower for JPEG XL), but WebP preset 6 files decode in 117.887 s (16.663 MP/s), about 2x faster than QLIC; QLIC encode is also about 5.6% slower than WebP preset 6 (585.964 s, derived).
compiler_and_flags: QLIC portable x86-64 Clang 22.1.4 Release build, no -march=native, no PGO; baseline encoders are the stock JPEG XL and WebP tools (versions not stated on the page)
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, Windows 11, one pinned logical processor, encode order rotated
tradeoffs: Lossless only. Not the decode winner: libwebp decodes this corpus about twice as fast, and encode time is close to WebP preset 6, not faster. Ships C/C++ SDK, CLI, Windows GUI and WIC plugin, a Rust decoder and a WebAssembly build; the Rust LZMS port keeps its MIT license. Very young project (first commit 2026-07-29, 1.0.0 on 2026-08-27).
caveats: Single-author benchmark of a three-month-old project. The speed win is measured against JPEG XL effort 9, an extreme setting: at JPEG XL effort 5 (629.126 s, 1,230,084,951 bytes) encode time is similar and QLIC output is 5.6% smaller (derived), and JPEG XL effort 1 to 3 are much faster than QLIC but 13% to 33% larger (derived). Encode and decode wall times include process startup and file I/O. Baseline tool versions and baseline flags not stated on the page. Measurements are Windows only. Benchmark harness is public in the benchmark directory (PowerShell scripts, pinned corpus manifest with SHA-256), so the run is reproducible in principle.
found_via: WebSearch 'Simple Lossless Image Codec SLI rANS CDF2sym github almost as fast as PNG better compression' listed OzzyMitchell/QLIC among lossless codec repos; also seen on github.com/topics/image-codec

name: oss-nvjpg
workload: Baseline JPEG decode to an RGB surface, 720x1080 (70 KiB file) and 3200x1800 (1.6 MiB file), average of 1000 iterations, on a Tegra X1 (Aarch64 Cortex-A57 at 2.091 GHz).
claimed_speedup: NVJPG hardware decoder: 2.036 ms vs libjpeg-turbo 6.127 ms (70 KiB image) and 15.997 ms vs 66.341 ms (1.6 MiB image); ratios about 3.0x and 4.1x (derived from page data). Also listed: stb_image with NEON 16.512 and 158.474 ms, Python-pillow 11.688 and 114.918 ms, nanoJPEG 48.299 and 531.575 ms.
hardware: Nvidia Tegra X1 SoC, Aarch64 Cortex-A57 at max 2.091 GHz (hardware JPEG block NVJPG)
tradeoffs: Drives the Tegra X1 hardware JPEG block (NVJPG) through the Host1x interface, so it only runs on Tegra X1 class devices (for example Nintendo Switch homebrew with devkitA64). Baseline JPEG only: progressive and arithmetic coded files return an error. Hardware YUV to RGB conversion and downscaling by up to 8. Requires C++20. GPL-3.0 limits reuse in permissive projects.
caveats: First-party README table only; no compiler, flags or libjpeg-turbo version stated, and the README does not say whether a timing harness ships in the repo. Two test images only. The speedup comes from dedicated hardware, not a better software algorithm, so it does not transfer to other CPUs. The libjpeg-turbo build is presumably NEON-enabled but this is not stated.
found_via: WebSearch 'GPUJPEG OR nvImageCodec JPEG decode throughput vs libjpeg-turbo images per second github benchmark' surfaced the oss-nvjpg reference; README opened on github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com

name: opencodecs
baseline: imagecodecs (Python wrappers over libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, OpenJPEG, libjxl and others) and tifffile for TIFF reading
workload: One codec operation per row at identical settings against imagecodecs 2026.8.16, on 4096x4096 uint16 and 2048x2048 RGB crops, median over fresh alternating processes; plus TIFF read of tifffile-written files against tifffile.
claimed_speedup: TIFF read versus tifffile on Linux: 4.2x (tiled deflate+predictor, 1 reader), 10.0x with 8 readers, 13.2x (3072x3072 uint8, 144 tiles, deflate, 8 readers). Versus imagecodecs: PNG RGB uint8 level 6 encode 3.45x (Mac) and 3.68x (Linux), JPEG quality 90 encode 2.68x (Mac) and 3.91x (Linux), JPEG decode 1.56x (Mac) and 1.80x (Linux), JPEG 2000 lossless threaded 4.66x to 8.05x, JPEG XL threaded 2.30x to 10x, BC7 decode 4.09x to 11x; TIFF LZW decode about 3x.
compiler_and_flags: wheels built as the project's CI wheels (flags not listed); benchmark script bench/bench_vs_imagecodecs.py
hardware: 20-core Apple silicon Mac, 64-core x86-64 Linux workstation (one 4-core group pinned) and a 4-core x86-64 Windows laptop; exact CPU models not stated
tradeoffs: Python package with 39 compiled codec extensions; most codecs wrap system or vendored C libraries (libjpeg-turbo, libwebp, OpenJPEG, vendored libjxl 0.11.2), so C++ users get the algorithmic parts only through the extension sources. Own kernels for LZW, PackBits, BC1 and BC7 decode. Parallel by default for JPEG 2000 and JPEG XL.
caveats: Many of the speedups come from threading by default versus a single-threaded baseline call (rows are marked 'opencodecs threaded'), from libdeflate under PNG (versus zlib), and from lower Python dispatch overhead. README lists many rows at 0.8x to 1.0x (zstd, brotli, lz4, WebP, QOI, JPEG-LS) and PNG decode 0.80x on Windows and 0.99x on Linux, so it is not a blanket win. Benchmark code is public, but CPU models are not named so the tier stays C. Linux JPEG XL lossy decode differs from imagecodecs output by 1 in about a third of values. Repository page shows 463 commits total and a v0.6.0 release on 2026-10-03.
found_via: GitHub topic page github.com/topics/jpeg-xl sorted by recently updated ('Native, parallel, cloud-aware image codecs for scientific imaging'), README Performance section

name: lowzag
baseline: libjpeg-turbo (progressive coefficient array memory); also ROM TJpgDec for decode time on ESP32
workload: Progressive JPEG decode at 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 scale of a 12-megapixel 4:2:0 image (peak allocation), plus decode time of progressive lowzag versus baseline TJpgDec on an ESP32-S3 at 240 MHz for 800x480, 1600x1200 and 4000x3000 test cards.
claimed_speedup: Memory at 12 MP: lowzag 36.2, 19.6, 6.8 and 3.4 MB at scales 1/1, 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 against libjpeg 36.1 MB at every scale (about 10.6x less at 1/8, derived from page data); with an 800x480 crop 3.4 to 2.3 MB. Decode time on ESP32-S3: 4000x3000 5.7 s vs 9.1 s for ROM TJpgDec baseline JPEG, 1600x1200 1.75 s vs 1.95 s, 800x480 0.63 s vs 0.46 s (slower).
hardware: ESP32-S3 at 240 MHz (timing table); memory numbers are allocation sizes, not tied to a CPU
tradeoffs: Progressive JPEG only, portable C99, decodes at 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scale without allocating the full coefficient array (keeps only the low-frequency corner its reduced IDCT needs); cropping and cancellation supported; ESP-IDF component. No arithmetic coding, CMYK or lossless JPEG; 8-bit, 1 or 3 components. Development is on a private GitLab with GitHub as mirror.
caveats: Memory numbers compare two different quantities (lowzag's own info.peak_alloc versus the coefficient array size libjpeg-turbo requests, computed from its JBLOCK size), as the README itself notes; process peak RSS is said to track both. The speed table is single measurements from one board and not reproducible on a host. This is a memory win, not a speed win: at 800x480 baseline TJpgDec is faster. Commit history shows an AI co-author. The README statement that mozjpeg, stb_image, Go image/jpeg and Rust jpeg-decoder also size progressive coefficient storage from the source dimensions comes from reading their source, not from measurement.
found_via: GitHub topic page github.com/topics/image-decoder sorted by recently updated ('Progressive JPEG decoder optimized for low memory')

name: PZP (Portable Zipped PNM)
workload: Load time of 500 COCO val2017 panoptic segmentation label maps (3-channel uint8 RGB, varying resolutions), in-process, best of 3 passes, libpzp.so called through Python ctypes with USE_COMPRESSION, USE_RLE and USE_PALETTE flags versus cv2.imread.
claimed_speedup: PNG total 1141.2 ms (2.282 ms per image) vs PZP 500.6 ms (1.001 ms per image): 2.28x faster load; files 4.1 MB as PNG vs 2.0 MB as PZP (52% smaller).
tradeoffs: Not PNG: a custom container (PNM pixel data wrapped in a compact binary header, ZSTD or LZ4, optional delta filter, palette indexing, inter-frame delta, multi-frame with audio) that needs libzstd and liblz4 and has no interoperability with PNG tools. Header-only C with Python ctypes bindings; 8-bit and 16-bit grayscale and RGB only. GPL-3.0.
caveats: First-party numbers with no CPU model, compiler or flags, and the harness is a Python script comparing a ctypes call against cv2.imread (OpenCV overhead is in the PNG column). The dataset is segmentation label maps with few distinct colors, which favour zstd with palette and RLE; the README itself gives this as the best case. The README credits the speedup to zstd decoding faster than zlib plus a flat layout, not to a faster PNG decoder. An optional SIMD (SSE2 and AVX2 prefix-scan) RLE decode path exists (compile-time INTEL_OPTIMIZATIONS) but is not what the headline number isolates. Not compared with fpng, Wuffs or libspng, which decode PNG much faster than libpng.
found_via: GitHub topic page github.com/topics/image-compression sorted by recently updated with C filter (README headline '2.28x faster to load than PNG')
